learn.diagramBlender.title: Where Claude and Blender work together
learn.diagramBlender.description: Everything happens on your own computer. Claude Code, in the desktop app or the terminal, writes a script. Blender runs the script in the background, with no window, and saves the model and pictures for Claude to look at. Claude Code on the web runs in the cloud, so it cannot reach Blender on your computer.

learn.diagramBuild.title: How a game gets built
learn.diagramBuild.description: Your game's code lives in a repository on GitHub. Claude makes a change on a branch, a copy for trying things. You look at what it changed. A pull request asks to add the change. While it is on the branch, your game does not change. The merge adds the change to the main game. GitHub then publishes it in a minute or two, and the game is live at its address.

learn.diagramParts.title: Where the Family Arcade lives
learn.diagramParts.description: The server familyarcade.eu in Germany sends the arcade to your tablet or phone once and keeps no log. Players, tickets and saves stay on your device, in the browser, and the arcade works offline after the first visit.
learn.diagramParts.server.title: familyarcade.eu

learn.diagramParts.device.noteThree: Works offline after the first visit
learn.diagramFriend.title: Opening a friend's game from the arcade
learn.diagramFriend.description: Tapping a friend's game in the arcade opens the game's own website, on the other family's GitHub Pages. The player's name and colour go along inside the link and never reach a server. The game's back button returns to the arcade.
learn.diagramFriend.arcade.title: The arcade, on your tablet
learn.diagramFriend.game.title: The friend's game
learn.diagramTogether.title: Playing together across homes
learn.diagramTogether.description: The Family Arcade's own connection service, on our server in Germany, passes the first hello between your tablet and your cousin's tablet, using the 4-letter code. It keeps no log. After that, the game's data travels directly between the two devices.
